workflow: Inbound receiving: scale tickets, sampling and grading
description: Trucks are weighed gross and tare at the elevator or receival site. Loads are probed and graded for moisture, test weight, foreign material and damage. The scale ticket, grade factors and discounts are keyed into the grain accounting receiving screen, which becomes the record for inventory, settlement and warehouse receipts.

workflow: Grower origination and contract booking
description: Merchandisers and buyers post daily bids, then negotiate cash, forward, basis and deferred-price contracts with growers by phone or at the counter. They key contract terms into the contract module and apply delivered tickets against open contracts.

workflow: Grower settlement, payables and warehouse-receipt reconciliation
description: Calculate and issue settlement checks with drying, shrink, storage and checkoff deductions and lienholders. Post to ledgers, reconcile book against physical inventory and warehouse receipts for examiner audits, and invoice buyers. All of this runs inside the grain accounting ERP.

workflow: Position, hedging and risk reporting
description: Roll physical contracts and inventory into a net position. Hedge on futures exchanges, reconcile the daily position report against broker statements, and report P&L and risk to management. At traders this runs in a CTRM. At elevators it is often a grain-accounting position report plus spreadsheets, which can be overlaid without replacing the core.

workflow: Outbound logistics and post-trade shipping documents
description: Schedule and load rail cars, barges, trucks and vessels against sales contracts. Prepare bills of lading, certificates and vessel nominations, and chase documents by email and PDF. Overlays such as Covantis and CommodityAI target this work and write back to the existing CTRM or ERP.

workflow: Market intelligence and price forecasting
description: Track weather, crop, trade-policy and supply-demand signals to set bids and basis, forecast prices, and brief traders and procurement teams. Today this happens in market-data terminals, analyst spreadsheets and newsletters, separate from the system of record.

workflow: Reservation-center booking and PNR servicing
description: Agents in airline contact centers create, change and cancel PNRs, check availability, quote fares, issue tickets and take payment for change fees or fare differences. They work in cryptic or graphical PSS screens. AI voice and chat agents can do this through PSS/NDC APIs without replacing the host.

workflow: Disruption rebooking and PSS queue work
description: Agents rebook, reroute and reissue tickets for passengers hit by delays, cancellations and misconnects. They work the PSS schedule-change, waitlist and ticketing-time-limit queues, then notify customers. Re-accommodation engines and AI agents can run on top of the PSS.

workflow: Airport check-in, boarding and departure close-out (DCS)
description: Counter and gate agents verify travel documents and APIS data, assign seats, print boarding passes and bag tags, handle standby, upgrades and oversales, board the flight and reconcile the passenger count with load control before departure. All of this happens in the DCS module of the PSS, which also transmits border data.

workflow: Fare filing, schedule and seat-inventory control
description: Pricing and revenue-management analysts load fares and schedules, file to ATPCO, and set booking-class (RBD) availability in PSS inventory. AI pricing engines can sit on top of the PSS. Moving to continuous pricing and native offers/orders means replacing PSS inventory with an offer and order system (FLYR, Amadeus Nevio).

workflow: Ticket exchanges, refunds and revenue accounting
description: Agents process exchanges, refunds and EMDs, applying fare rules and waivers by hand when auto-pricing fails. Revenue-accounting clerks reconcile ticket sales against flown coupons and settle BSP/ARC agency debit memos. Most of this work sits in separate revenue-accounting systems fed by PSS ticket data.

workflow: Bag acceptance and mishandled-baggage tracing
description: Staff accept and tag checked bags at check-in and transfer them to loading areas. Agents take lost-bag reports, trace bags in WorldTracer and arrange delivery or interim expense payouts. These baggage systems are separate from the PSS and exchange data with it.

workflow: Order entry, routing and execution
description: Brokers and dealers take client and house orders and enter them into the trading front end (ODIN, NOW, an OMS or EMS). They run pre-trade checks, route orders to the exchange, and record fills. The front end sits on exchange connectivity and broker risk management that the legacy trading stack provides.

workflow: Trade booking, allocation, confirmation and books and records
description: Executed trades are booked into the back office (Broadridge BPS, FSS FLEX, MPC S21 BOFIS). Staff allocate them to accounts, confirm them with clients and counterparties, and run them through the overnight batch that updates the official books and records.

workflow: Clearing, settlement and asset servicing
description: This covers novation and settlement with the CCP and CSD (CHESS, VSDC, KSEI C-BEST, CDSL/NSDL), managing fails, and transferring securities. It also covers corporate actions, fee and commission calculation, and client statements produced from the core subledger.

workflow: Position and cash reconciliation and break resolution
description: Each day, staff match the core's positions and cash against custodian, clearing-house, prime-broker and bank statements, then investigate and clear the breaks. Much of this runs on spreadsheets and email, or on overlay tools such as Duco or AccessFintech.

workflow: Margin, collateral and risk-limit monitoring
description: Staff calculate and meet CCP initial and variation margin, monitor client margin and collateral, and track intraday positions against risk and credit limits. Breaches are escalated to traders.

workflow: Regulatory transaction reporting, trade surveillance and compliance
description: Staff produce trade and transaction reports (CAT, EMIR, MiFIR, exchange and SEBI/OJK filings), fix rejected submissions, run trade and e-comms surveillance and trade reconstruction, and support audits. The work runs off data pulled from the core.

workflow: Chargeback and dispute handling
description: Work issuer and acquirer dispute queues: take the cardholder claim, pull transaction and merchant evidence, apply Visa/Mastercard reason codes, give provisional credit, and file chargebacks, representments or pre-arbitration within network deadlines. Mostly runs in dispute tools and network portals beside the card core.

workflow: Network settlement reconciliation and exception handling
description: Reconcile daily Visa/Mastercard settlement and clearing files against the authorization log and general ledger. Then investigate unmatched, duplicate and late presentments, post manual adjustments and close out-of-balance items.

workflow: Fraud alert review and card blocking
description: Review fraud-scoring alerts and suspicious-transaction queues, contact cardholders to verify activity, block or reissue cards, and log confirmed fraud for scheme reporting and loss recovery.

workflow: Cardholder and merchant servicing and account adjustments
description: Handle calls and chats about declines, fees, balances and lost or stolen cards, post supervisor-approved fee reversals and goodwill credits, and work early-stage collections, all through the card core's servicing screens.

workflow: Card application underwriting, merchant onboarding and issuance
description: Decide card applications and set credit limits, underwrite and KYB merchants for acquiring, then set up accounts, MIDs and plastics (embossing, PIN mailers, returned mail) in the processor.

workflow: Core processor configuration, scheme mandates and compliance evidence
description: Load network bulletins and mandated rule changes (interchange tables, BIN ranges, reason codes) into the COBOL/mainframe or licensed processing configuration, regression-test the batch and online cycles, fix defects, and gather PCI DSS and scheme-compliance evidence for auditors.

workflow: Subcontractor and supplier invoice entry with job cost coding
description: Key supplier and subcontractor invoices into AP. Code each line to job, cost code and cost type. Three-way match against PO, subcontract and delivery tickets, then route for PM approval and release payment once compliance documents are in. Overlays such as Field Materials and Adaptive post coded invoices into Vista, Foundation or Sage, so the core GL can stay.

workflow: Field timecards and construction/certified payroll
description: Collect foremen's crew timecards and enter hours by job, phase and cost code. Apply union rates, prevailing wage and fringes, run multi-state payroll, and file certified payroll (WH-347) and union remittance reports. Payroll can be replaced by tools such as Miter or Trayd that sync job-costed labour back to the existing GL.

workflow: Progress billing, retainage, lien waivers and collections
description: Prepare monthly AIA G702/G703 pay applications (UK and AU: valuations and progress claims) against the schedule of values, including retainage and stored materials. Exchange conditional and unconditional lien waivers. Chase overdue receivables and retention at closeout. Billing overlays such as Siteline work alongside the ERP's AR ledger.

workflow: Change orders and monthly cost-to-complete review
description: Price change orders with the PM, log pending and approved COs, and update contract and budget values. Then hold the monthly job cost review, which refreshes cost-to-complete, projected margin and percent complete per job. Most of the work happens in spreadsheets and PM tools (Procore, Clearstory) beside the ERP's job cost module.

workflow: Month-end close, WIP schedule and surety/lender reporting
description: Close the general ledger and post percentage-of-completion revenue and over/under-billing adjustments. Produce the WIP schedule and financial statements for bonding companies, lenders and auditors (UK: cost value reconciliation). The GL and revenue recognition live in the system of record, so replacing this workflow means replacing the core.

workflow: Job setup and contract/commitment master data
description: Set up new jobs: enter the contract, original budget, cost-code structure, tax jurisdiction and subcontract and PO commitments. This master data drives every downstream posting and report, so changing it means changing the core.

workflow: Loan intake, appraisal and approval
description: Interviewing members, collecting documents, field appraisal of farms and small businesses, credit analysis and loan-committee approval. Usually runs on a separate LOS, paper forms or spreadsheets and then posts to the core.

workflow: Delinquency follow-up and repayment collection
description: Phone calls and repeat field visits to overdue borrowers, negotiating rescheduled repayment plans, and recording collection status against loan accounts.

workflow: Teller counter transactions and end-of-day cash balancing
description: Deposits, withdrawals, passbook updates and loan repayments posted straight to the core ledger at the counter, then branch cash reconciliation against system totals and field collection sheets.

workflow: Member onboarding, KYC and member service
description: Opening member accounts and share accounts, collecting ID and KYC documents, answering member questions by phone or chat and fixing account problems. Digital-onboarding and AI contact-centre overlays can sit on top of the core here.

workflow: Interest, dividend and general-ledger posting and reconciliation
description: Computing and posting loan interest, penalties and dividends on member shares, reconciling the core ledger with bank statements and field collections, often with side spreadsheets. The ledger lives in the core.

workflow: Portfolio-at-risk, provisioning and regulatory returns
description: Extracting loan and deposit data from the core to compute PAR, loan-loss provisions and capital ratios, then filing returns to the cooperative regulator or apex body (NCUA call report, OJK, RBI/NABARD, BSP, SKM).

workflow: Branch teller transactions and cash-drawer balancing
description: Cash and cheque deposits, withdrawals, transfers, cashier's cheques and loan payments keyed at the counter into the core's teller front end. Includes end-of-shift drawer balancing and vault counts.

workflow: Account opening, KYC and AML alert review
description: Interview customers, collect and verify ID and due-diligence documents, key customer and account data into the core CIF, and run credit checks. Downstream, review transaction-monitoring and sanctions alerts and write up suspicious activity.

workflow: Contact-center and branch servicing: queries, disputes, record maintenance
description: Answer balance, fee and statement questions. Handle disputed transactions and card blocks. Keep customer records current (address, signatories, dormancy, deceased estates). Agents work several core screens and green-screen inquiry functions.

workflow: GL, suspense and clearing reconciliation, payment exceptions and regulatory returns
description: Each day, reconcile GL suspense, nostro/vostro and clearing accounts against core extracts. Repair failed payments and clear returned items. Compile regulatory and central-bank returns from core extracts and spreadsheets.

workflow: Loan origination, servicing and collections
description: Take applications, run credit analysis, document collateral and route approvals. Book and disburse the loan on the core loan module. Service schedules and payoffs. Work delinquent accounts through repayment plans and repossession.

workflow: Core ledger, end-of-day batch and product-parameter maintenance
description: Run and monitor end-of-day and end-of-month batch. Fix batch failures and interest or fee calculation exceptions. Change product parameters. Maintain COBOL, RPG and FLEXCUBE code on the system of record. Taking this work away means replacing the core.

workflow: Filing intake, review and docketing
description: Take in paper and e-filed pleadings, check them for required forms, signatures and fees, reject or flag deficient filings, then open the case and docket entries (case number, parties, events) in the case management system of record.

workflow: Courtroom record, minutes and transcription
description: Capture what happens in court: verbatim record and transcripts by court reporters or stenographers, plus clerk minute entries, rulings and dispositions keyed into the case system. AI transcription such as Adalat AI can sit on top of the system without replacing it.

workflow: Judicial research, bench memos and order drafting
description: Judges and research attorneys read the motions and pleadings, research the law, and draft bench memos, tentative rulings, opinions and orders. Clerks then issue the orders. Copilots such as Learned Hand read from the case system but do not replace it.

workflow: Calendaring, hearing notices, reminders and public inquiries
description: Build dockets and calendars, coordinate hearing dates, send notices and court-date reminders, and answer litigant and public questions about case status. Overlays such as eCourtDate read from and write back to the case system.

workflow: Fines, fees and payment-plan collections
description: Receipt filing fees, fines, restitution and bail, set up payment plans, chase delinquent accounts, and trigger failure-to-pay actions. The financial ledger and disposition records live in the core case management system.

workflow: Evidence and discovery review for criminal cases
description: Defenders and prosecutors pull, review and summarise discovery (body-cam video, interrogations, records) and organise exhibits for trial. This sits next to the court system and agency case systems, and AI tools such as JusticeText and TrialKit work as overlays.

workflow: Clinical documentation (nursing flowsheets, physician notes, discharge summaries)
description: Nurses chart assessments, vitals and care notes. Physicians write H&Ps, progress notes and discharge summaries. Much of this is copied forward or dictated and transcribed into the EHR. This is the main target for ambient AI scribes, which write notes back into Epic, Oracle or MEDITECH without replacing them.

workflow: Orders, medication reconciliation and pharmacy verification (CPOE / MAR / BCMA)
description: Physicians enter orders and reconcile home medications. Pharmacists verify orders and handle interaction alerts in the pharmacy queue. Pharmacy technicians maintain profiles and dispense. Nurses administer and scan at the bedside. Order entry, the medication record and alert logic live inside the core EHR database, so changing this workflow means changing the core.

workflow: Patient registration, ADT and scheduling (patient administration system)
description: Front desk and ED registrars capture demographics and insurance and verify eligibility. Staff schedule tests and appointments, handle admission, discharge and transfer, and fix duplicate MRNs. This runs on the PAS or master patient index (HBCIS, SAP IS-H, Epic Cadence/Prelude, Millennium). Replacing the PAS is the core replacement event, as with SAP's IS-H end of support in 2027-2030 and Queensland's HBCIS.

workflow: Coding, CDI, charge capture, prior authorization and HIM/release of information
description: Coders abstract finished charts into ICD-10, CPT and DRG codes and query physicians. Billing staff capture charges and work claim edits and denials. HIM staff scan outside records, chase incomplete charts and release information. AI coding, CDI and prior-auth tools read from the EHR and write back without replacing it.

workflow: Care coordination: results inbox, handoffs, discharge planning and referrals
description: Clinicians review and route results and portal messages, hand off at shift change and coordinate with consultants. Social workers and case managers plan discharges, place patients in SNF or home health, fax referral packets and book follow-up. Much of this runs over phone, fax and spreadsheets alongside the EHR. AI agents (patient outreach, capacity and discharge tools) sit on top of the EHR.

workflow: EHR build, interfaces and legacy system maintenance
description: Hospital IT analysts and programmers configure order sets, flowsheets and reports. They maintain HL7/FHIR interfaces and patch legacy code (MUMPS in VistA and MEDITECH MAGIC, CCL in Millennium, ABAP in SAP IS-H). They also plan data migration when the core is replaced. This is where shrinking skills bite, for example VA's retirement-eligible MUMPS programmers.

workflow: Order intake, entry and order-status service
description: Customer orders arrive by phone, email, PDF, fax or EDI exception. Staff re-key them into the ERP order-entry screen, check price, stock and credit, then answer status, backorder and delivery calls. Overlays can read and write ERP orders through its APIs, so this can be automated without replacing the core.

workflow: Quoting, contract pricing and inside/outside sales
description: Reps build quotes from spec sheets, BOMs, blueprints and RFQs, apply customer contract prices and rebates held in the ERP pricing matrix, then follow up to convert quotes to orders. AI overlays (quote generation, takeoff, cross-sell) read ERP price and stock data without replacing it.

workflow: Purchasing, replenishment and supplier expediting
description: Buyers review min/max and reorder reports from the ERP, cut POs, negotiate with vendors, and chase acknowledgements and late shipments by email. Agentic procurement layers sit on top of the ERP's PO records.

workflow: Receiving, picking, shipping and inventory control
description: Receive freight against POs, put away, pick and pack from ERP pick tickets or RF screens, ship, then run cycle counts and post adjustments. Perpetual inventory quantities and valuation live in the ERP ledger, and Eclipse, P21 and BisTrack ship native RF/WMS modules. Fully replacing this workflow means replacing the core inventory system of record.

workflow: Accounts payable three-way match
description: Match vendor invoices against the PO and the ERP receiver, resolve price and quantity discrepancies with buyers, and release invoices for payment. AP automation overlays post approved invoices back into the ERP.

workflow: Billing, cash application, credit holds and collections
description: Invoices come out of ERP ship confirmations. Clerks apply customer remittances to open invoices, make collection calls, and place or release credit holds on orders. Cash-application and collections tools overlay the ERP's AR ledger.

workflow: Production planning, MRP and scheduling
description: Planners take MRP output and turn it into a sequence of jobs on each work centre. They expedite hot orders and rebalance capacity, often in Excel outside the ERP, then push revised schedules and work orders to the floor. Advanced planning and scheduling tools and AI planners can sit on top of the ERP and write back planned orders, so the core can stay in place.

workflow: Purchasing and supplier follow-up
description: Buyers act on MRP messages, cut purchase orders and chase suppliers for confirmations and late material. They manage shortages and resolve receiving discrepancies. Most of this happens in email and spreadsheets around the ERP's PO tables, so agent overlays (Didero, Magentic, Mandel, Traza) can take it over without replacing the core.

workflow: Quoting, order entry and promise dates
description: Estimators quote jobs from drawings, BOMs and emailed RFQs. Inside-sales and order clerks re-key customer POs (PDF, fax, email, EDI) into the ERP, check availability and commit ship dates. AI order-entry and quoting tools (Endeavor, Smartbase, Uptool, Workist) read the documents and write sales orders into the existing ERP.

workflow: Shop-floor reporting, material movement and inventory transactions
description: Workers record labour, quantities completed and scrap against work orders. They issue and backflush components, move WIP, receive and put away purchased parts, ship finished goods and reconcile system on-hand to the floor. These transactions are the ERP's inventory and WIP ledger. An MES or app can capture them, but replacing the record itself means replacing the core.

workflow: Inspection, nonconformance and corrective action
description: Inspectors run first-article, in-process and final checks, record results and write nonconformance reports. Quality managers drive disposition and corrective action, and receiving inspection is checked against POs. This work often lives in a separate QMS or on paper tied to ERP lots, so it can be modernised without a core swap.

workflow: BOMs, routings, engineering change and job/standard costing
description: Engineers maintain bills of material and routings and push engineering changes through. Cost accountants close out job costs, analyse labour, material and overhead variances against standard, and roll new standard costs. BOMs, routings and cost roll-ups are the ERP's master data and valuation logic, so changing them structurally means replacing the core.

workflow: Service request intake, triage and work order creation
description: Customers, tenants or operators report a breakdown by phone, text, portal or a 311-style request. Staff check urgency, asset, warranty and contract status, then raise a work request or order in the EAM/FSM. Today this runs on call centres, email and re-keying into Maximo, SAP PM notifications or ServiceTitan. AI intake agents (Avoca, Netic) answer and book, then write into the existing system of record, so the core stays in place.

workflow: Dispatch and daily crew scheduling
description: Assign work orders to technicians and crews by skill, location, parts and priority, then reshuffle the board around emergencies and no-shows. Planners often export from Maximo or SAP to Excel or a whiteboard and never write the result back. AI dispatch (Probook) and contractor coordination (Prefix) sit on top of the FSM/CMMS through APIs.

workflow: Preventive and predictive maintenance planning
description: Maintain PM schedules, job plans, meter and condition triggers on the asset hierarchy, then build and level the backlog into weekly schedules. PM masters, job plans and the asset hierarchy live inside the EAM (Maximo PM/Job Plans, SAP PM maintenance plans), so a full replacement means migrating the core. Condition-monitoring vendors (Tractian, Augury, Infinite Uptime, Groundup.ai) feed triggers into it.

workflow: On-site diagnosis, repair and work order close-out
description: Technicians diagnose faults, repair or replace parts, and close the work order with labour hours, parts, failure codes and findings. They often use paper tickets that the office re-keys, or thin mobile clients (Maximo Mobile, SAP Service and Asset Manager, Fieldreach). Troubleshooting copilots (Edmund) and field-execution tools (FYLD) are overlays that write back to the EAM.

workflow: MRO parts, storeroom inventory and procurement
description: Look up part numbers, reserve and issue stock against work orders, reorder from suppliers, and receive and reconcile deliveries. Storeroom, item master and purchasing are integrated with ERP finance (SAP MM/PM, Maximo Inventory and Purchasing), so replacing this means touching the core system and the ERP.

workflow: Asset register, inspection and compliance records
description: Keep the asset register and hierarchy, meter readings, inspection results, defect and nonconformity history, and the regulatory evidence auditors ask for (CAMO records, safety inspections, refrigerant logs). This is the system of record itself. MTA OIG found NYC Transit still loading substation assets into its EAM years into the rollout. Inspection-capture vendors (Scope, Trendspek, Gecko Robotics) feed it.

workflow: Bank, subledger and balance sheet reconciliation
description: Each period, staff match bank statements, subledgers (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll) and balance sheet accounts to the GL. Most of this happens in spreadsheet tie-outs exported from the ERP. They then investigate and clear reconciling items. Overlays such as BlackLine, Numeric, Stacks and Ledge sit on top of the GL and read from it, so this work can be automated without replacing the core.

workflow: Journal entries, accruals and period-end adjustments
description: Staff prepare accruals, prepaids, reclasses, allocations, depreciation and revenue recognition entries, usually built in Excel and uploaded to the GL. They then post entries and produce the trial balance. Agents can draft and post entries through the ERP's APIs or upload templates. The GL stays the book of record.

workflow: Flux and variance analysis and financial reporting
description: Staff compare actuals with the prior period and with budget, then write variance commentary. They build financial statements and management or board packs from GL extracts. This is read-only work on top of the ledger.

workflow: Intercompany, consolidation and FX translation
description: Staff reconcile intercompany balances, book eliminations and run currency translation. They then build the consolidated package, often in Hyperion HFM or in spreadsheets fed by several entity ledgers. Shadow-GL overlays such as Nominal do this alongside the existing ERPs, so it does not require replacing the entity GLs.

workflow: Close management, review sign-off and audit support
description: Controllers run the close calendar and checklist, and review and approve entries and reconciliations. They maintain internal controls (SOX/ICFR) and answer external auditors' prepared-by-client requests and sample pulls. Close-management tools such as FloQast and Numeric overlay this work on any ERP.

workflow: GL system of record: chart of accounts, posting engine, period control and ERP migration
description: This is the ledger itself. It covers chart of accounts and cost-center structure, subledger posting rules, period open and close, the audit trail, and statutory localizations. It also covers the multi-year work of migrating from SAP ECC, Oracle EBS, JD Edwards, Dynamics GP or Tally to a new ERP. Greenfield AI-native ERPs (Rillet, Campfire, DualEntry, Light) compete here and require a full migration.

workflow: Application intake, data entry and document verification
description: Take paper, phone and portal applications, key them into the eligibility system screen by screen, and fix data that did not carry over from the portal. Then request, scan and index verification documents (pay stubs, IDs, leases) and check them against data matches (wages, SSA, IRS). Overlays (navigators, AI form-fillers, document intake) can take this over while the core stays in place.

workflow: Eligibility determination, benefit calculation and authorization
description: Run the rules engine to determine eligibility and compute benefit amounts, override or work around system errors, and authorize payment. In legacy cores (COBOL, Model 204, Curam, Deloitte IE) the rules and the payment calculation live in the system of record, so replacing this means replacing the core.

workflow: Renewals, redeterminations and change reporting
description: Contact recipients before renewal and periodic-report deadlines, collect updated income and household information, process reported changes, and keep coverage from lapsing. Outreach and verification layers (AI voice agents, navigation apps, payroll-data verification) sit on top of the core. The final recalculation still runs in the core.

workflow: Call center, case status inquiries and referrals
description: Answer call center and lobby questions about case status, missing documents, benefit amounts and notices people did not understand. Refer clients to employment, child support and community services. This work can be fully overlaid by chat and voice agents that read case status from the core.

workflow: Fraud, overpayment recovery, quality control and appeals
description: Investigate suspected fraud and overpayments, establish claims, and set up repayment or recoupment from ongoing benefits. Review sample cases for quality control, generate and correct notices, and prepare evidence for fair hearings that decide appeals. Recoupment and corrected payments must be posted in the core ledger.

workflow: Policy rule changes and legacy code maintenance
description: Turn annual statutory changes (rates, thresholds, new programs such as H.R.1 work requirements) into code in COBOL, Model 204 or Curam rule sets. Run parallel and regression tests and keep batch payment runs going. The rules are hard-coded and often undocumented, so this work is the core system itself.

workflow: Application intake and completeness check
description: Clerks take permit and license applications from paper, email or the portal. They check that each one is complete, key applicant, contractor and parcel data into the permit system, then open a case number or send a deficiency letter.

workflow: Plan and land-use review
description: Plans examiners and planners review drawings, site plans and land-use proposals against building, zoning and fire codes. They write markup comments, route the file to other departments, and record approve, revise or deny in the case.

workflow: Inspection scheduling and field inspection
description: Staff take inspection requests and build daily routes. Inspectors visit sites, record pass or fail with photos and correction notes on paper or a tablet, then enter the results into the permit record.

workflow: Complaint and code enforcement case management
description: Officers investigate complaints on site and decide whether a violation exists. They issue notices of violation, track compliance deadlines, and prepare cases for hearings. These cases live in the same land-management system as permits and parcels.

workflow: License issuance, renewals and fee collection
description: Staff calculate fees from the fee schedule and take payments. They verify qualifications, insurance and prior violations, issue or renew licenses and permits, send renewal and lapse notices, and reconcile receipts to the ledger.

workflow: Applicant questions and status inquiries
description: Counter, phone and email staff answer questions about requirements, fees and case status. They look the case up in the legacy screens and explain the next steps.

workflow: Paper return, payment and correspondence intake and data capture
description: Mailroom and data-entry staff open paper returns, payments and letters, scan them, and key line items into the tax processing system. At the IRS staff keystroke every digit of paper returns, with about 22% transcription errors. OCR or ML extraction can sit in front of the core and emit e-file XML, so the master file does not have to change.

workflow: Return validation, error resolution and account adjustments
description: Examiners work error and exception queues for returns that failed validation (math errors, mismatched IDs, missing schedules), correct data, send notices, and decide abatement, penalty waiver and reasonable-cause requests. The validation rules and the account postings live in the master file or integrated tax system.

workflow: Taxpayer contact centre and account inquiries
description: Agents take calls and messages about balances, notices, refunds and payment plans, look up accounts across several legacy screens, and record the interaction. AI agent-assist overlays exist (CDTFA with SymSoft Axyom Assist) and read the core without replacing it.

workflow: Audit selection, examination, non-filer discovery and refund fraud screening
description: Auditors select cases, match returns against third-party data, run desk and field audits, and propose assessments. Fraud teams screen flagged refunds for identity theft and hold or release them. Analytics overlays (Palantir at IRS CI, Quantexa at HMRC, Deckard for local occupancy tax) sit on top of the core data and do not replace it.

workflow: Payment posting, delinquent account collection and revenue reconciliation
description: Payment staff post lockbox and electronic payments, research misapplied payments, and reconcile deposits and distributions to the general ledger. Collections officers chase delinquent accounts, set up installment agreements, and file liens and levies. Posting to the taxpayer account ledger is a core function. Collection case management can be a separate system, as Denmark's failed EFI was.

workflow: Local property valuation, exemptions and assessment roll maintenance
description: County and municipal assessors inspect parcels, process deeds and transfers, vet homestead exemptions, and update values on the assessment roll held in the CAMA system. AI overlays (TrueRoll, C3 AI) work beside CAMA. AI-native CAMA replacements (CAMAai) are only at the pilot stage.

workflow: First notice of loss and claim setup
description: Staff take the first report of a loss by phone, email, web form or app. They key the loss details into the claims system, check the policy is in force, and create the claim and its first reserve. Liberate, Assured and Avallon automate this step with voice and digital AI agents, but the claim record itself still has to be written to the system of record.

workflow: Coverage check and claim investigation
description: An adjuster compares the policy terms, limits and exclusions with the facts of the loss. They contact the insured, the claimant and witnesses, and gather police, medical and property evidence to decide liability. This work happens in documents, phones and email around the claims core, so it can be automated without replacing it. AI-native TPAs (Reserv, ClaimSorted, Elysian, Strala) take over this whole step.

workflow: Damage appraisal and repair estimating
description: A field or desk appraiser inspects the damaged vehicle or property, or reviews photos of it. They write an estimate in an estimating tool such as CCC or Xactimate, agree the cost with the repairer or decide on a total loss, and re-enter the totals into the claim file. Overlay AI (Tractable, Finch, Agentech QA review) works on the estimate, not the core.

workflow: Reserving, settlement and claim payment
description: Adjusters set and revise reserves within their authority limits and negotiate the settlement. Staff then issue payments to verified payees, lienholders or mortgagees. Reserves and payments are the financial ledger of the claims system of record, and they feed reinsurance, actuarial and regulatory reporting. Replacing this step means replacing the core.

workflow: Claim file documentation, indexing and record review
description: Claims assistants index incoming mail, photos, invoices, medical records and bills into the claim file, update the diary, and summarise long records for the handler. This is the main target for document-AI and back-office agents (Pace, Curant.ai, Wisedocs, Agentech file review). These tools read from and write to the existing claims system through its screens or APIs.

workflow: Fraud referral, recovery and litigation management
description: Adjusters flag suspicious files and refer them to SIU. Recovery staff pursue subrogation and salvage. Litigation specialists and paralegals manage defence counsel, records, mediations and trials. Overlay analytics vendors (Shift, CLARA, Owl.co, Consint.AI) score files on top of the core, and legal work runs in separate matter-management tools.

workflow: New business intake and policy issuance
description: Staff take applications and submissions from agents and brokers (ACORD forms, emails, spreadsheets), check the data, key it into the policy system, collect the first premium, and issue the policy with its declarations and forms.

workflow: Risk evaluation, pricing and referral
description: Underwriters read submission documents and third-party reports, check exposure already in force, decide to accept, decline or modify, set rating and endorsements, and arrange reinsurance for large risks. AI underwriting workbenches can do this as an overlay without replacing the core.

workflow: Policy changes, cancellations, reinstatements and renewals
description: Service staff handle midterm endorsements (coverage, beneficiary, address), non-pay cancellations, reinstatements and the renewal cycle. Each change is written into the policy record and the required notices go out.

workflow: Policyholder and agent service contacts
description: Reps answer calls, emails and chats about coverage, documents and billing. They look up the policy across legacy screens, log the interaction and route anything they cannot resolve. Voice and chat AI agents can take this over through integrations with the core.

workflow: Premium billing, collections and commissions
description: Staff invoice premiums, post payments, reconcile agency statements, work out refunds and adjustments, and pay agent commissions. Billing is often a module of the legacy policy system or tightly coupled to it.

workflow: Product, rate and rule changes and regulatory reporting
description: Actuaries design products and rates. Programmers then code the new rates, rules and forms into the policy system (often COBOL or RPG), test them, and produce statistical and regulatory extracts from policy data.

workflow: Specimen receipt, requisition intake and order entry
description: Staff receive specimens with paper, faxed or electronic requisitions. They match tubes to orders, key patient, test and insurance data into the LIS, apply barcode labels, and chase problem specimens (missing orders, mislabels) with collection sites. AI requisition OCR (MarginLogic, Onymos, CrelioHealth) can feed clean orders into the existing LIS without replacing it.

workflow: Result review, autoverification, release and critical-value calls
description: Technologists review analyzer and manual results, apply delta and range checks, order repeats or dilutions, enter non-interfaced results (microscopy, micro plates), then verify and release them to the EHR. They phone critical values and document read-back in the LIS. The autoverification rules and the result of record live in the LIS, so moving this workflow means replacing the core.

workflow: Quality control, calibration and instrument maintenance
description: Staff run and record daily QC and calibrations, review Levey-Jennings charts, document corrective actions, perform preventive maintenance, and log instrument downtime. Most of this sits in middleware and QC software (Data Innovations, Bio-Rad Unity) next to the LIS, so it can change without replacing the core.

workflow: Anatomic pathology case tracking, diagnosis and report sign-out
description: Histology and cytology staff track blocks and slides and assemble cases. Pathologists examine slides, dictate or type reports, and sign them out, and secretaries transcribe and route the reports. AI-native entrants (elea, Voquill) target this workflow with voice-driven reporting and aim to replace the AP LIS outright. Digital pathology overlays (Proscia, PathAI, Techcyte) sit beside it.

workflow: Send-out testing, CPT coding and lab billing
description: Staff package send-out tests for reference labs, build manifests, and re-key returned results. They also assign CPT/ICD codes, check billing data and work denials, usually in a separate lab RCM system interfaced to the LIS. Interface-level automation and AI coding can replace this without touching the LIS of record.

workflow: LIS build, interfaces, validation and accreditation records
description: LIS analysts maintain the test dictionary, rules and instrument/EHR interfaces. They validate every change and upgrade (CAP GEN.48500, ISO 15189) and support downtime. Lab managers keep accreditation and inspection documentation. This work is the system of record itself.

workflow: Document intake, fee receipting and indexing
description: Deeds, mortgages, releases and transfers arrive over the counter, by mail or by e-recording or e-lodgement. Staff check and receipt fees, assign a document or instrument number, scan the document, and key grantor/grantee, document type, parcel ID and legal description into the index of the register.

workflow: Examination, registration and requisitions
description: Examiners check each lodged instrument for legal sufficiency (execution, notarisation, legal description, chain of title, registrability under the land titles statute) against the current register. They then update the title register or ownership record, issue certificates of title or recorded copies, or send rejection notices and requisitions to lawyers and conveyancers and process corrected resubmissions. Caveats, court orders and fraud holds are noted on titles.

workflow: Title search, certified copies and public enquiries
description: Title searchers, abstractors, conveyancers and the public search the index and images, pull chains of title and encumbrances, and order certified copies. Registry counter staff help with searches and microfiche retrieval. Private title plants and AI overlays (Landeed, Dono, Titl, Orbital) sit on this read-only layer.

workflow: Cadastral mapping and boundary maintenance
description: Mapping staff update the cadastral or parcel map in GIS for subdivisions, splits, merges and boundary adjustments from lodged plans, plats and surveys. Surveyors verify boundaries in the field and help resolve discrepancies.

workflow: Back-file conversion and redaction
description: Historical deed books, plat books, microfilm and paper titles are scanned, indexed and quality-checked for loading into the register. Personal identifiers are redacted from images. Examples: 25M titles in the Philippines LTCP, and Kofile and Balcony county archive projects.

workflow: Ownership change feed to assessor and tax office
description: After registration, ownership changes and sale prices go to the assessor and tax office (in the US, often as transfer-tax declarations). Assessor staff check transfers, reconcile owner names and legal descriptions against parcel records, and correct mismatches.

workflow: Application intake and borrower origination contact
description: A loan officer or interviewer takes the application by phone, branch or web, keys it into the LOS, pulls credit, quotes rates and answers borrower questions. Voice and point-of-sale AI agents (Sela, Tidalwave) work in front of the LOS and do not replace it.

workflow: Document processing, verification and underwriting
description: Processors collect and index borrower documents, verify employment and third-party items, and clear conditions. Underwriters and credit analysts assess income, DTI, credit and collateral, then approve, suspend or decline. AI document and underwriting agents feed the existing LOS.

workflow: Closing, funding, post-closing and boarding to servicing
description: Closers prepare disclosures and loan documents, coordinate with title and settlement agents, and fund the loan. Post-closing staff check file completeness and ship files to investors. Boarding staff map loan terms from the LOS into the servicing system. All of this happens inside the LOS system of record, so taking it over means replacing the LOS (Fuse, Lama AI).

workflow: Payment processing, custodial reconciliation and escrow administration
description: Servicing staff post borrower payments, research exceptions and reconcile custodial accounts. They pay property taxes and insurance from escrow and run annual escrow analyses. All of this runs as batch processing on the servicing core (e.g. ICE MSP), so replacing the workflow means replacing the core (ValonOS, Sagent Dara).

workflow: Borrower servicing calls and inquiries
description: Reps handle calls about payoff quotes, statements, payments and escrow, and record each interaction in the servicing system. Voice and text AI agents (Kastle) answer these calls and write back to the existing core.

workflow: Collections, loss mitigation and default management
description: Staff call delinquent borrowers, collect financials and negotiate repayment plans, forbearance or modifications. They also refer accounts to foreclosure or bankruptcy attorneys and prepare investor default reporting. AI collection agents (Salient) sit on the lender's servicing core.

workflow: Overnight batch scheduling, monitoring and abend recovery
description: Operations staff watch JCL batch job streams in schedulers such as CA-7, Control-M and TWS. They restart or rerun abended jobs from the correct checkpoint using run books, run backups and DR, and log incidents for vendors and internal IT.

workflow: Transaction entry and correction on 3270/CICS screens
description: Business users re-key paper forms, faxes and emailed spreadsheets into green-screen CICS/IMS entry panels field by field. They then work edit and error reports to fix rejected or suspended records and re-enter the corrections.

workflow: Customer and case inquiry lookups across mainframe screens
description: Staff answer phone, email and walk-in inquiries by moving across several 3270 screens to find account, policy or case records. They copy values into notes, emails or CRM tickets, and pull historical records and screen prints when auditors ask.

workflow: Batch output reconciliation and spreadsheet reporting
description: Clerks reconcile daily batch output reports and control totals against downstream ledgers and partner files, and chase out-of-balance items. They export spool and flat-file reports and rebuild them in Excel for management and regulatory reporting.

workflow: COBOL/JCL change, documentation and production support
description: Developers make small COBOL and JCL changes for rules, rates and table updates, test them and promote them through change control. They document undocumented programs and fix production abends. AI documentation and agentic TN3270 tools (Hypercubic, Kodesage, Swimm, IBM watsonx Code Assistant for Z) sit here without replacing the system of record.

workflow: Rewrite, re-platform and data migration off the mainframe
description: Teams extract business rules and analyse dependencies, then convert or rewrite COBOL/PL/I/JCL to Java or cloud and migrate VSAM, IMS and Db2 data. They prove behavioural equivalence and manage a multi-year program with integrators. Mechanical Orchard, AWS Transform, CloudFrame and Zengines target this work, which replaces the core system of record.

workflow: Patient access: registration, eligibility and prior authorization
description: Front-desk and call-center staff collect demographics and insurance, check eligibility and benefits on payer portals or by phone, and get prior authorizations. They record coverage, copay and deductible on the account in the PM/ADT module before the visit. This is the main source of later denials.

workflow: Medical coding and clinical documentation review
description: Coders read the clinical record and assign ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS codes, modifiers and inpatient DRGs. They query physicians when documentation is unclear. Autonomous-coding vendors work alongside the core, reading notes from the EHR and writing codes back.

workflow: Charge capture, claim build and submission
description: Staff reconcile charges against the chargemaster and schedule, then build claims (837/UB-04/CMS-1500 or the national payer equivalent). They scrub them against payer edits, fix clearinghouse rejections and resubmit. The chargemaster, claim engine and patient account ledger live in the core billing system (Epic Resolute, Soarian, MEDITECH, IS-H, TrakCare).

workflow: Claim follow-up, denials and appeals
description: A/R and denial staff work worklists of unpaid, underpaid and denied claims. They check claim status on payer portals or by long phone calls, find the root cause, add records and file appeals. Managers watch aging and denial trends. Agentic and voice-AI vendors mostly sit here, on top of the core's work queues.

workflow: Remittance posting and cash reconciliation
description: Payment posters load ERA/835 remittances and key in paper EOBs and lockbox checks. They post payments and contractual adjustments to patient accounts and reconcile deposits to the bank. Posting writes to the account ledger in the core system of record.

workflow: Patient statements, payment plans and self-pay collections
description: Patient account reps send statements, answer billing calls, set up payment plans, take payments and send unpaid balances to collections. Patient portals (MyChart, HealthHub) put bill-pay in front of the core billing data.

workflow: Borrower inquiries and payment calls
description: Inbound calls and chats about payments, escrow changes, payoffs, statements, PMI and servicing transfers. Agents look up and update the account on servicing screens (for example MSP green screens). AI voice agents (Kastle, ICE's own MSP agents) now sit on top of this work.

workflow: Collections and loss mitigation
description: Outbound calls to delinquent borrowers, promises to pay and repayment plans. Hardship packages are collected and reviewed for forbearance, modification or deferral eligibility under investor and CFPB Reg X rules. Decision logic often sits in bolt-on tools (Black Knight Loss Mitigation, Brace/Stavvy) that read from and write to the core.

workflow: Payment posting, escrow and tax/insurance disbursement
description: Daily cash posting and suspense research. Custodial account reconciliation. Annual escrow analysis, and payment of property tax and hazard insurance from escrow. Force-placed insurance on lapse. ARM rate changes and payoff quotes. These are the system-of-record calculations inside MSP, LoanServ or Phoebus.

workflow: Foreclosure, bankruptcy and REO management
description: Referring loans to foreclosure and bankruptcy attorneys, tracking state-specific timelines and milestones, ordering property inspections and preservation, and preparing affidavits and lien releases. This runs largely in default modules and attorney-network portals attached to the core.

workflow: Investor reporting, remittance and loan boarding
description: Monthly reconciliation and remittance to Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Ginnie Mae (RFS) and private investors, and clearing reporting exceptions. Transferred-in loans are boarded by mapping prior-servicer data and fixing exceptions. CFPB found transferees manually overriding fields the platform rejected. Any change here triggers Ginnie Mae RFS testing.

workflow: Complaints, QWRs and regulatory inquiries
description: Researching and answering qualified written requests, notices of error, and CFPB, state and ombudsman complaints within statutory deadlines. Also call-monitoring QA for TCPA, FDCPA and UDAAP. The work pulls account history from the core but runs in case-management tools.

workflow: Time-to-pay payroll run (gross-to-net)
description: Each pay cycle, staff collect timesheets, overtime and attendance exceptions and key them into payroll. They run pre-payroll variance checks, compute gross-to-net, fix discrepancies, issue pay and payslips, and process off-cycle, retro and correction payments. The calculation and the pay ledger live in the core payroll engine.

workflow: Hire-to-retire employee master data
description: Staff enter new hires, terminations, transfers, promotions, leaves and pay rate changes from paper or emailed forms into HR and payroll records. They also run onboarding paperwork such as I-9 or right-to-work checks and keep personnel files. These records form the system of record that payroll reads.

workflow: Payroll tax, statutory filings and reconciliation
description: Staff prepare and file payroll tax returns and statutory contributions (W-2 and 941, RTI and P60, STP, PPh 21 and BPJS, EPF, CPF, SSS). They reconcile payroll to bank and GL, process garnishments, keep tax tables current, and produce year-end forms. Filings are generated from the payroll ledger.

workflow: Employee pay, leave and policy inquiries
description: HR and payroll staff answer employee questions about pay, deductions, leave balances, benefits, tax forms and policy by phone, email, ticket and in person. They also handle employment verifications. An overlay can read the HRIS without replacing it.

workflow: Benefits enrollment and carrier reconciliation
description: Benefits staff enroll employees in health, pension and savings plans and key elections. They send deduction and eligibility files to carriers and reconcile carrier invoices against enrollment and payroll deductions. Much of this runs in separate benefits platforms and spreadsheets that feed deductions to payroll.

workflow: Pay codes, award and union rule configuration
description: Analysts and compensation staff maintain pay codes, allowances, tax tables, awards and collective-agreement rules in the payroll engine and test their effect on pay. Queensland Health needed 1,507 SAP customisations for this layer. This is the logic that makes cores hard to replace.

workflow: Employer contribution intake and reconciliation
description: Staff receive employer contribution files, payroll census data or paper schedules, then key or load them into the core member ledger. They reconcile the files against bank receipts and correct misallocated contributions with backdated adjustments. In 401(k) TPAs the same work covers brokerage statements, census and payroll files, and trust accounting.

workflow: Employer arrears, inspections and recovery
description: Staff chase employers for late, missing or short contributions and calculate late-payment penalties. They run payroll inspections or audits to find under-declared wages, and refer defaulters for legal recovery. In the national provident funds (EPFO, KWSP, BPJS Ketenagakerjaan, SSS) this is a large enforcement unit. Arrears cases can be managed outside the core, but penalties and arrears post back to it.

workflow: Member service: calls, counters and complaints
description: Contact-centre and counter staff answer member questions about balances, statements, eligibility and withdrawals. They log complaints about statement or interest errors and route cases to back-office teams. Staff read from the core but rarely write to it, so AI agents and member apps can take this work without replacing the core.

workflow: Withdrawal, retirement, death and disability claims
description: Benefit officers verify identity and supporting documents for retirement, death, disability and special withdrawals (housing, medical, education). They check eligibility under scheme rules, calculate the payout or pension (DB accrual, tranches, protections) and authorise payment. The calculation and payment run inside the core system of record.

workflow: Member and employer registration, onboarding and data maintenance
description: Staff register new employers, plans and members, and update names, nominees and bank details from forms. They investigate and merge duplicate accounts and handle job-change transfers. In US 401(k) this includes plan setup and moving plan provisions between TPA document systems and recordkeepers.

workflow: Benefit payment runs, interest crediting, statements and regulatory reporting
description: Finance staff run pension payroll and lump-sum payment batches, reconcile bank payment files and handle returned payments. They run annual interest or dividend crediting and produce member statements. They also pull data for regulatory, actuarial and board reports, often by assembling spreadsheets.

workflow: Vessel stowage and berth planning
description: Planners build load and discharge plans and crane splits from BAPLIE and other carrier EDI, then negotiate berth windows with lines and agents when vessels arrive off schedule. The work happens in the TOS planning client (for example the N4 vessel planner), but AI overlays already plug in without replacing the core: Loadmaster stowAI, Portchain Connect, Avlino PortBerth.

workflow: Yard allocation and housekeeping planning
description: Yard planners set stacking strategies and allocate block and slot positions. They manage congestion and schedule housekeeping and reshuffle moves to cut rehandles. Optimisation overlays such as Avlino YardSight, Loadmaster stackAI and Westwell ReeWell read TOS data and push plans back, so the planning layer can change without replacing the system of record.

workflow: Equipment dispatch and move execution
description: Control-room staff dispatch quay cranes, RTGs, straddles and terminal tractors from the TOS job lists (for example N4 XPS/ECN4). Operators carry out each move from vehicle-mounted terminals, and controllers fix exceptions such as a wrong location, a missing box or a breakdown, usually by radio. This is the real-time container inventory and job engine itself, so changing it means replacing the core TOS. Fernride and Westwell autonomous tractors still take their jobs from it.

workflow: Gate transactions and container checking
description: Gate clerks and checkers process trucks against appointments and verify container numbers, seals and damage, either at the gate or on the quay and in the yard. They then key or confirm each in-gate, out-gate, discharge or load transaction in the TOS and fix mismatched records. Each confirmation writes the container's custody and location to the system of record, so automating it fully (OCR, auto-gate) still runs through the core TOS.

workflow: Booking, release, EDI and customs-hold documentation
description: Documentation staff take bookings, delivery orders, releases and customs or agency holds from EDI, portals and email, and fix rejected EDI messages. They coordinate inspections, plus reefer, dangerous-goods and out-of-gauge handling records. Much of the work is re-keying and exception handling around the TOS, which document AI and integration layers can take over without replacing the core.

workflow: Terminal billing, tariff disputes and productivity reporting
description: Billing staff compile handling, storage, demurrage and reefer charges from TOS event history, invoice lines and consignees, and handle tariff disputes. Managers produce moves-per-hour and dwell-time reports and reconcile vessel move counts with lines after departure. The work reads TOS events but usually runs in a billing module, an ERP or BI tools, so it can be rebuilt without replacing the core.

workflow: Invoice capture, coding and 2/3-way match
description: AP clerks receive vendor invoices by mail, email or PDF, key header and line data into the ERP, code them to GL accounts, and match them to POs and goods receipts, resolving price and quantity variances. Ardent's 2025 survey found that 48.6% of invoices still arrive by non-electronic means. Capture and matching tools sit on top of SAP ECC, Oracle EBS or JDE without replacing them.

workflow: Vendor inquiries, statement reconciliation and duplicate-payment recovery
description: AP staff answer supplier calls and emails about payment status and remittance. They reconcile vendor statements against the AP ledger and look for duplicate payments, missing credits and fraud. Overlay AI tools such as Xelix read ERP data without replacing the ERP.

workflow: Requisition intake, approvals, PO creation and expediting
description: Employees raise purchase requests, and staff chase approvers by email. Buyers turn requisitions into POs and send them to suppliers, then track and expedite late orders. Intake and orchestration layers (Zip, Lio, Didero, Eezee) sit in front of the ERP and post POs back into it.

workflow: Supplier sourcing, RFQ/RFP events and negotiation
description: Procurement staff find and evaluate suppliers, run RFQ and RFP events, analyse bids, and negotiate prices, terms and contracts, including tail-spend and spot buys. This work runs in sourcing suites or spreadsheets next to the ERP, so AI sourcing and negotiation tools (Levelpath, Pactum, Arkestro, Mercanis, Aerchain, Procure AI) do not need the core replaced.

workflow: Vendor master onboarding and payment runs
description: Staff onboard suppliers and maintain the vendor master, including tax IDs, bank details and callback verification against fraud. They prepare payment runs, choose invoices for early-pay discounts or holds, and release payment files to the bank. The vendor master and payment program live in the ERP (SAP FI-AP, Oracle Payables, JDE), so moving this workflow means moving the system of record.

workflow: Goods receipt, received-not-invoiced accruals and AP close
description: Receiving staff inspect deliveries and post goods receipts or report shortages and damage. At month-end, accountants book accruals for goods received but not yet invoiced and reconcile the AP subledger and aging to the GL. Goods receipts and GL postings are core ERP transactions, as Birmingham's failed bank reconciliation and year-end misallocations showed.

workflow: Checkout, tender and returns at the register
description: Ring up items by scan or weight, apply promotions, coupons and loyalty, take cash, card or vouchers, issue receipts, and handle returns, exchanges and refunds with manager overrides. Every step posts a sales transaction to the POS, which is the fiscal record of sale.

workflow: Till close, cash office and deposit reconciliation
description: Count drawers at shift open and close, reconcile tills to the POS Z-report, log overages and shortages, and prepare the bank deposit and safe log. This work reads POS totals, but cash-management tools can be layered on top without replacing the POS.

workflow: Receiving, cycle counts and inventory adjustments
description: Check vendor and DC deliveries against the PO or ASN, post receipts, shortages and damage claims, run cycle counts and the annual count with handhelds, and post variances and shrink adjustments to the merchandising system's stock ledger. RFID, vision and handheld overlays can take over much of this work.

workflow: Store replenishment, stocking, planogram and shelf price execution
description: Review and adjust the suggested store order, then transmit it. Fill shelves from the backroom, reset fixtures to planograms, print and hang shelf labels and promo signs from the weekly price batch, and audit shelf price against the scan price. AI ordering tools (e.g. fresh replenishment) sit on top of the core.

workflow: Merchandise planning, allocation, markdown and promotion pricing
description: Export sell-through and stock reports, usually to Excel. Plan open-to-buy and allocation, decide markdowns, promotions and price changes, and key the resulting price events back into the merchandising system. This is the main target for AI decision overlays (planning, assortment and pricing agents) that leave the core system in place.

workflow: Item master setup, vendor terms, purchase orders and deal reconciliation
description: Create SKUs in the item master from vendor spreadsheets (cost, retail, UPC, hierarchy, tax code, supplier link), negotiate cost and allowances, raise POs, and reconcile vendor deal claims, chargebacks and invoices. The item master and cost records are the merchandising system of record, so automating this end to end means replacing or deeply re-platforming the core.

workflow: Registration, records and registrar service desk
description: Registrar and records staff answer student and parent questions by looking across SIS screens. They process add/drop and override forms, key prerequisite, capacity and time-conflict overrides, place or lift holds, and process FERPA releases and name/address changes. All of these are writes to the core student record.

workflow: Admissions application and transcript intake
description: Admissions and enrollment clerks key application, transcript and residency data from forms and PDFs into a new student record and verify the supporting documents. This usually happens in a CRM or admissions front end (Slate, Element451) that feeds the SIS, so it can be automated without replacing the core.

workflow: Master schedule and timetable building
description: Schedulers build the term or annual master schedule, assigning sections to rooms, times and instructors and resolving conflicts by hand, often in a spreadsheet before loading the result into the SIS. Overlay tools such as Coursedog and Scientia do this outside the core.

workflow: Attendance, grading and academic standing
description: Teachers and attendance clerks record daily attendance, call parents about absences and enter excuse and truancy codes. Faculty enter term grades, and registrar staff post grades, process grade changes and incompletes, and recalculate GPA and standing. These are the SIS's core transactional records and drive state funding counts.

workflow: Advising, transfer credit and degree audit
description: Advisors and evaluators enter transfer credit equivalencies, run degree audits and patch exceptions by hand. They meet students to plan courses, flag at-risk students and clear them for graduation. Overlays such as EdVisorly, Risely AI and degree-audit tools read from and write rules back to the SIS without replacing it.

workflow: State, federal and government compliance reporting
description: Institutional research and district data staff extract enrollment, demographic and completion data from the SIS, clean and reconcile it in Excel, and submit statutory returns (IPEDS, CALPADS and other state counts, the HESA/DfE census, the PDDikti Feeder, AISHE). This sits downstream of the core and is automatable by analytics or reporting layers such as Doowii, Scout and SEVIMA GoFeeder.

workflow: Customer care for bills, plans, outages and cancellations
description: Agents take inbound calls and chats about bills, plan changes, outages and cancellations. They toggle between CRM, billing and network screens, log the interaction and offer retention deals. This is the main target of AI care agents that sit on top of the existing BSS (Sierra at Liberty Global, Wonderful at Bezeq).

workflow: Order capture, activation, number porting and order fallout
description: Retail, phone and online reps key in activations, upgrades, moves and number ports. They check serviceability, assign numbers and SIMs and submit orders to provisioning. Fallout teams chase orders stuck between CRM, provisioning and billing and re-key them by hand (the target of Totogi BSS Magic).

workflow: Bill disputes, credits and adjustments
description: Billing specialists check disputed charges against usage and rating records. They issue credits or adjustments within approval limits and tell the customer the outcome.

workflow: Collections, payment arrangements and suspend/restore
description: Collections agents work the delinquency queue. They call customers, set up payment arrangements and trigger suspension or restoration of service in the billing system.

workflow: Bill-cycle operations, rating and price-plan configuration
description: Billing operations and IT staff run bill cycles, review rating exceptions and sample bills, and hold or correct accounts before bills go out. They also set up new price plans, bundles and promotions across the catalog, rating and CRM, then test them. All of this sits inside the core billing and charging engine.

workflow: Install and repair dispatch and work-order closure
description: Dispatchers schedule technicians for installs and repairs from work orders created in the BSS. Technicians do the physical work and close the order with equipment serials, which feeds activation and billing.

workflow: LC issuance, advising and amendment
description: Staff re-key import LC applications from client forms or portal PDFs into the trade engine, check the wording, and release MT700. They authenticate and advise incoming export LCs, process MT707 amendments, and track beneficiary acceptance and the outstanding liability. The instrument is booked in the legacy system of record.

workflow: Document examination and discrepancy handling
description: Staff log and scan presented documents (bills of lading, invoices, insurance, certificates of origin) and check them against LC terms, UCP 600 and ISBP. They record discrepancies, negotiate waivers or refusals by MT734/MT799, phone and email, and archive the paper originals. AI checkers (Traydstream, Cleareye, TradeSun, Conpend) work as overlays that feed results back into the engine.

workflow: Sanctions, dual-use and trade-based money laundering screening
description: Staff screen LC parties, vessels, ports and goods against sanctions and dual-use lists, check prices for TBML red flags, investigate hits and document the outcome. This usually runs in a separate screening tool linked to the trade engine.

workflow: Bank guarantees and standby LCs
description: Staff draft and issue guarantees and SBLCs (MT760), negotiate non-standard wording with legal and the client, track expiry and reductions, and handle claims and extend-or-pay demands. The liability lives in the trade system of record.

workflow: Facility limits, booking and settlement
description: Staff check each transaction against the client's trade facility, margin or collateral and get approval for any excess. They book fees, FX and accounting entries, process reimbursement claims and payments (MT103/MT202), and reconcile nostro accounts. All of this is posted inside the engine and core banking.

workflow: Client advisory, onboarding and service
description: Relationship managers and service desks advise corporates on structuring and pricing LCs, collections and guarantees, gather KYC and financials, and answer status queries. This work runs through bank portals and CRM, not the booking engine.

workflow: Meter read to bill (read capture, validation, bill exceptions)
description: Meter reads arrive from walk or drive routes, handhelds, or AMI. Reads with high, low or estimated consumption are verified, then the bill run executes. Billing analysts work the held-bill exception queue, fixing reads, rate codes and account setup before release. The rating and billing engine is the core of the CIS, so automating this end to end means replacing or re-platforming the core.

workflow: Customer contact: high-bill inquiries, complaints and account questions
description: Call-centre and walk-in staff answer questions about high bills, usage history, payment arrangements and outages, using CIS screens. They log the contact, adjust bills or refer disputes onward. AI agents and portals can sit on top of the existing CIS without replacing it (for example Gigawatt Bill Analyzer at AEP, POWERCONNECT.AI, SEW, and Kraken with Sierra).

workflow: Start, stop and transfer service, and field service orders
description: Staff key start, stop and transfer-of-service orders for move-ins and move-outs, including deposits and final bills. The CIS then generates field orders for connects, disconnects, meter exchanges and investigations, which dispatchers schedule and technicians close. Account, premise and service-agreement records live in the CIS, so this workflow sits on the core data model.

workflow: Credit and collections: arrears, payment arrangements and disconnection
description: Collections staff work aged-debt lists, send shutoff notices and set up payment arrangements. They apply protections such as medical certificates and winter moratoria, then order disconnections and reconnections. Dunning strategy and outreach can be run outside the CIS. The CIS keeps the account balance and issues the disconnect order.

workflow: Payment posting and daily cash reconciliation
description: Staff post lockbox, agent, card and online payments to accounts, fix misapplied and returned payments, and reconcile daily cash to the general ledger. Payment processors such as InvoiceCloud and Paymentus already sit outside the CIS and post back to it through batch files.

workflow: Tariff configuration and regulatory reporting
description: After a rate case or tariff decision, staff configure the new rates and riders in the CIS and run parallel test bills. They also compile reports for regulators on billing, disconnections, arrears and complaints. Rate logic is held in the billing engine, which is why legacy CIS owners cite slow tariff changes as a reason to replace it. Duke's testimony says new rates are time-consuming to implement in its old CIS.

workflow: Inbound receiving and putaway
description: Unload inbound trailers, check quantities and condition against the ASN or PO, label pallets with license plates, key receipts and damage into the WMS, then move pallets to system-directed putaway locations.

workflow: Order picking, packing and shipping
description: Pickers follow RF-gun or paper prompts to locations and confirm each pick by scan. Packers pack, weigh and label cartons, shippers manifest with the carrier and generate bills of lading, and loaders sort and load outbound trailers.

workflow: Inventory control, cycle counting and slotting
description: Run cycle counts, investigate location and quantity variances, post adjustments in the WMS, maintain item and location master data, and run slotting analysis, often in Excel, to place fast movers near shipping.

workflow: Wave planning, labor assignment and training
description: Shift supervisors plan and release pick waves, assign people and equipment to zones based on volume and cutoff times, rebalance labor during the shift, and train new and temporary workers on RF screens and safety.

workflow: Dock appointment scheduling and yard management
description: Book carrier appointments, assign doors and yard slots, sequence trailer loading, and handle late or unscheduled trucks by phone and email. This often runs in a separate dock or yard module or in spreadsheets beside the WMS.

workflow: Exception handling, interface failures and carrier claims
description: Resolve short picks, wrong locations, WMS-to-ERP and carrier interface failures, and shipment damage claims. This often means re-keying orders or inventory transactions by hand and chasing carriers and suppliers across portals.

workflow: Daily position, transaction and cash reconciliation
description: Operations analysts match positions, transactions and cash in the portfolio accounting book of record (Axys, APX, InvestOne, TRUST 3000, Avaloq) against custodian and bank feeds. They research breaks and post correcting entries. Goldman's InvestOne alone keeps a shadow book across 40+ custodians.

workflow: Corporate actions, security pricing and cost basis
description: Staff process dividends, splits, mergers and voluntary elections. They fix the tax lots and cost basis these change, validate vendor prices and manually price illiquid holdings. All of this happens in the accounting engine's security master and lot records.

workflow: Performance measurement and client reporting
description: Reporting teams calculate returns, check holdings and performance for errors, and assemble quarterly client report packages. Reports are often built with REPLANG on Axys/APX or from data extracts, and overlays such as Addepar or Masttro can replace this step without touching the book of record.

workflow: Client review, planning and rebalancing
description: Advisors and portfolio managers prepare for and hold client reviews, document meetings, check model drift and cash needs, and generate and submit rebalancing trades. AI meeting and planning tools (Jump, Zocks, Nevis, Saturn) sit on top of the CRM and accounting data here.

workflow: Alternatives and private-fund data capture
description: Analysts collect capital calls, distributions, NAV statements and K-1s from GP portals and email PDFs, then key them into the accounting system. Document-extraction overlays (Canoe, Arch) feed clean data into the core instead of replacing it.

workflow: Account onboarding, money movement and fee billing
description: Staff collect account paperwork, initiate ACATS and other transfers, set up accounts and fee schedules, and process withdrawals and journals with callback checks. They also calculate AUM-based fees and produce invoices or custodian debit files.
